description:
Credit Controller & Accounts Assistant

London Permanent Hybrid working £33k - £36k Per Annum

The organisation

Our client is an established UK property consultancy working across complex, high-value assets. The business has ambitious growth plans under its current leadership and is investing in a Finance function that is increasingly visible across the organisation.

Rather than operating solely as a back-office function, Finance works closely with colleagues, clients and external stakeholders. This makes the Credit Controller & Accounts Assistant position particularly suited to someone who enjoys building relationships alongside working with financial information.

The team has a sociable culture with regular events and offers:

Study support.
An annual bonus, paid at the end of the financial year.
Pension contributions matched up to approximately 6.5%.
Private medical insurance.
Hybrid working, with a minimum of three days per week in the London office.

Chasing overdue debts by telephone and email while maintaining positive client relationships.

A working knowledge of credit control, accounts assistance or a related finance function.
Experience allocating cash receipts or working with sales and purchase ledgers.
Good written and verbal communication skills.
Confidence communicating with internal and external stakeholders.
Excellent attention to detail and an organised approach to managing competing priorities.
Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel and other Microsoft applications.
Reliability and a commitment to completing work accurately.
Experience using accounting systems, with NetSuite knowledge particularly advantageous.
Reconciliation experience, where possible.

Experience within property or professional services would be useful but is not essential, and candidates from other sectors are encouraged to apply.

This Credit Controller & Accounts Assistant opportunity would suit someone looking to build their finance career within a growing organisation while gaining exposure beyond traditional credit control.

You'll get great exposure across the business, working with international customers, colleagues in the US, manufacturing partners in Asia and teams across Sales, Planning and Supply Chain. You'll be close to the full process, seeing how customer requirements translate through purchasing and production and ultimately through to delivery.

But the real opportunity is to make the role your own. The team is looking for someone who will spot where things could work better, bring ideas and solutions and help shape new ways of working rather than simply following processes that have always been there.

You'll have plenty of autonomy and the chance to use your judgement. Priorities can change quickly and problems won't always have an obvious answer, so this will suit someone who's naturally curious, asks the right questions and enjoys working out the best way forward.

For someone who wants to broaden their experience, get closer to different areas of an international business and have a genuine voice in how a growing function develops, there's a lot of opportunity here.

The Role

Day to day you'll be:
- Coordinating international customer requirements through purchasing, production and delivery.
- Supporting forecasting and planning to keep customer requirements, purchasing and production aligned.
- Working with international teams and overseas manufacturing partners to coordinate purchasing and production.
- Making sure orders are accurate, with the right quantities, information and required dates.
- Tracking production and supply, identifying potential delays or issues and finding solutions.
- Working closely with Sales, Planning, Supply Chain and Procurement.
- Building strong customer relationships and providing clear, accurate updates.
- Managing different customer and market requirements.
- Finding practical solutions when timings, quantities or production requirements create challenges.
- Keeping product, customer and supply information accurate.
- Looking for ways to improve processes and make things work better.

The Person

There are several backgrounds that could work well here. You may come from international customer or commercial operations, or your experience might sit closer to buying, merchandising, planning, production or supply chain.

What's important is that you've had exposure to both the customer side and some of what happens further upstream to make those orders possible.

That could include:
- Working with international customers, wholesale accounts or distributors.
- Working with overseas suppliers, factories or manufacturing partners.
- Purchasing, production or supply coordination.
- Critical paths, lead times, stock and availability.
- Planning, forecasting or working closely with planning teams.
- Coordinating across Sales, Supply Chain, Operations or other internal teams.
- Identifying problems, working through the options and finding practical solutions.

You don't need every one of these, but you should understand that getting a customer order right involves more than processing it and arranging delivery.

This also isn't a pure supply chain or production role. You'll work closely with international customers and commercial teams, so you'll need to be a confident communicator who enjoys building relationships as much as getting into the detail.

You'll need to come from a product-led environment such as consumer goods, FMCG, retail, fashion, beauty, homeware or something similar.

Above all, we're looking for someone who thinks ahead, joins the dots and takes ownership. Someone with good judgement, strong attention to detail and the confidence to spot when something doesn't quite add up and work out what to do about it.

If you're looking for a busy, varied role where you'll be trusted, challenged and given the opportunity to put your stamp on something, I'd love to hear from you.

Because you'll actually get to do the marketing.

You'll have genuine ownership, creative freedom and the opportunity to see your ideas move from a scribble on a page to a finished campaign in the real world.

You'll work closely with decision-makers, have the freedom to experiment and play a meaningful part in shaping the future direction of the brand.

You will be responsible for handling a high volume of calls from our service users, so an excellent telephone manner is essential.The ability to organise, manage, and take responsibility for your own workload is integral to being successful in this role. title: Receptionist

The post-holder will be responsible for dealing with telephone calls and checking patients in with their appointments, helping patients with their queries and undertaking admin tasks in the Practice. The role is suitable for someone who has admin and primary care work experience and they must be able to multi-task, hold excellent communication skills and has a passion for helping patients and able to provide excellent customer service. The main role of the receptionist is to receive, assist and direct patients and visitors in the Practice in a professional, courteous, and effective way. The individual must be able to provide general assistance to the Practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and visitors, both in person and via telephone. The individual must also be able to support the Practice team by supporting and undertaking in administrative duties. Reception duties: 1) Ensure an effective and efficient reception service is provided to patients and any other visitors to the Practice. 2) Deal with all general enquiries, explain procedures and make new and follow-up appointments. 3) Using your own judgment and communication skills ensure that patients with no prior appointment but who need urgent consultation are seen in a logical and non-disruptive manner. 4) Explain Practice arrangements and formal requirements to new patients and those seeking temporary cover and ensure procedures are completed. 5) Receive and make telephone calls as required. Divert calls and take messages, ensuring accuracy of detail and prompt appropriate delivery. 6) Action repeat prescription requests and ensure that they are ready for collection by the patient within 48 hours, in line with Practice protocol. 7) Take action on clinicians requests for further information/patient contact information etc. (including computerised practice notes), ensuring completion of all associated paperwork. 8) Advise patients of relevant charges for private (non-General Medical Services) services, accept payment and issue receipts for same. 9) Enter patient information on to the computer as required. 10) Prepare clinical rooms for surgeries, supply prescription forms and record numbers in use and ensure adequate supplies of consumables (including bottles, couch rolls, test request forms etc.).
